metadata.title: Darren Waller Showing Great Red-Zone Chemistry with his QB
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller has shown a strong connection with Bryce Young in his first two games with the Panthers, making an immediate impact after joining the team in August. He didn't play in the preseason, but when the games started to count, he became a prime option for Carolina in the red zone. Waller had a short touchdown called back due to a penalty in Week 1, but he found the end zone twice in Week 2. The 34-year-old caught all five of his targets for 61 yards in his two games and will continue to be a go-to option in the red zone due to his ability to win contested catches. He only played 35% of the team's snaps in Week 1 and 44% of the snaps in Week 2, so there is also the potential for more growth in other areas of the field as he settles into the team's offense. Waller is definitely a tight end on the rise and is a pickup to consider in all formats if you need tight end help. This week, he and the Panthers visit the Browns in Cleveland.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) a non-participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: To no surprise, Carolina gave Waller the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go for Week 3 at this point.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Has Played His Way onto 12-Team Rosters
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller made the most of limited work Sunday, catching all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-3 win over Atlanta. The touchdowns will get the attention, but the role still needs some context. Waller played 29 offensive snaps, or 44%, while Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans both played more. That was still a step up from Week 1, when Waller logged 24 snaps and had a touchdown wiped out by penalty. Carolina clearly has a use for him near the goal line, and this is not new territory. Waller scored six times on only 24 catches for Miami last season. The volume may stay frustrating, but tight end is thin enough that those scoring chances matter. RotoBaller's Week 3 waiver coverage has him as an add in 12-team leagues, with one column calling him a must-add at that depth. He is worth picking up now, but managers should expect some low-target weeks along the way.

metadata.title: Darren Waller snags two touchdown passes in win
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two scores in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller had himself a great fantasy day, heavily boosted by the two touchdowns. He's only had five targets so far this year, but if the Panthers are willing to use him in the red zone, he's worth a look for those needing a tight end streamer.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Two TD grabs in rout of Atlanta
metadata.description: Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller had a touchdown called back in Week 1 against the Bears on an offensive pass interference, but he made a pair of red-zone catches count in this one, scoring from seven and 12 yards. It's become evident that Carolina has big plans for Waller in the scoring area this season. He's not going to go for many yards most weeks, but he's always a candidate to get into the end zone. Waller gets a plus Week 3 draw against the Browns next Sunday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Boom-or-Bust Tight End Option Vs. Atlanta
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 receiving yards in last Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears. The 34-year-old did have a one-yard touchdown called back on a penalty. Waller signed a one-year, $1.3 million contract with the Panthers during training camp and did not play a preseason game. He will look to build chemistry with quarterback Bryce Young as he continues to learn Carolina's offense. The veteran TE is a boom-or-bust option in fantasy as he rotated with Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans throughout Week 1. Waller logged 24 snaps compared to Tremble's 34 and Evans' 27. Waller is touchdown-dependent and is an option in very deep leagues, and is RotoBaller's TE32 in the latest Week 2 rankings.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) returned to practice as a full participant on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, the veteran tight end was back and practicing at full capacity for the Panthers on Thursday. He should play in Week 2 but shouldn't be considered a reliable fantasy option at this point in the season.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (rest) misses practice on Wednesday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (rest) missed Carolina's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: To no surprise, the veteran tight end was given the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go in Week 2, although he shouldn't be started in most league formats at this point after a disappointing start to the season last week.

metadata.title: Darren Waller catches two passes in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Waller made the most of his minimal involvement in a Carolina passing attack that saw the ball spread to seven different receivers in the season opener, averaging 14.0 yards per reception in the loss. The tight end will look for more involvement in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Goes for 28 yards in Week 1
metadata.description: Waller secured both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller actually had a one-yard touchdown called back on a penalty on the Panthers' opening drive. Carolina used all three of Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Waller pretty heavily against Chicago, and both Tremble and Waller each ran 18 routes. Waller isn't going to be a full-time player, but it's clear he's going to be featured in the scoring area. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet most weeks and gets a road date with the Falcons next Sunday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Suiting up Sunday
metadata.description: Waller is listed as active for Sunday's season opener against the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Waller had been preparing to play Week 1, and he will indeed occupy a spot on the active roster. It remains to be seen what role he will fill, though, as fellow tight ends Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Feleipe Franks will also be in uniform.
